title: Self-Storage Fundamentals
description: How self-storage works and who our customers are, every unit type and size, the facility and its locks, how a site earns money, protection, the rental agreement, the delinquency ladder and the lien process, auction day, the lines you never cross, running the site safely, and the privacy rules that protect tenants and Greens. Course 2 of the Greens Storage Academy.
overview: Why people rent, how long they stay, and every unit size and type
The facility, the roll-up door, gates, locks and overlocks
Rates, occupancy, fees and California late-fee math
Protection, and the rental agreement with California's SB 709 disclosures
Greens' delinquency ladder, lien law in California and Texas, and auction day
The lines you never cross, running the site, safety and privacy
tags: self-storage, new hire, lien, rental agreement

lessons.title: Greens Site Hours and Access
lessons.summary: Office and gate hours for each Greens site, how gate codes work, and when Cubby changes a delinquent tenant's gate code.

questions.q: A Valley Center caller is leaving a one-bedroom: a queen bed, a couch, a dresser, a small table and about 25 boxes. She needs no aisle. What do you suggest?
questions.explanation: A one-bedroom with about 25 boxes is the classic 10x10. A 10x15 is right only if she wants an aisle; a 5x10 is a studio.

questions.q: A customer asks how much floor a 10x15 gives her. What do you tell her?
questions.explanation: Width times depth: 10 x 15 = 150 square feet. 100 is a 10x10; 300 is a 10x30.

questions.q: A new Escondido tenant offers you a spare key "just in case." The right answer is to decline it, even if you would log it.
questions.explanation: The tenant keeps the only key; that is exclusive control, and why storage creates no bailment. Logging a spare does not make holding it right.

questions.q: A Murrieta tenant says his roll-up door is heavy and will not stay up. What do you do?
options: Tell him to lift from a corner
Take the curtain out of the guides
questions.explanation: A door that will not stay up has lost spring tension. Springs under tension can break a wrist; they are a trained technician's job. Lifting by a corner twists the curtain.

questions.q: Which units get an overlock? Pick all that apply.
options: A delinquent unit Cubby flags Overlock Needed
A paid unit after an argument at the counter
questions.explanation: Overlocks go on flagged delinquent units, vacant units and rented units found unlocked. Never on a paid-up unit, whatever happened at the counter.

questions.q: A Fairfield tenant's code was refused at 11:00 PM, and Cubby's log shows "outside of hours." What do you do?
questions.explanation: Gate hours end at 10:00 PM, so a refusal at 11:00 PM is not a broken code. Never give out a master code.

questions.q: A man at the Temecula counter says he is a tenant's brother and needs the gate code for some tools. He is not on the account. What do you do?
options: Give it, since he knows the unit
Read it with the tenant on speaker
Let him in on your own code
questions.explanation: A gate code is a password, and even the fact that someone rents is private. Knowing a unit number proves nothing, and your own code is logged as you.

questions.q: A tenant parks his trailer in a painted fire lane "for an hour" while he unloads. What is right?
options: Ask him to move it now
Fine while the gate is open
Only the fire department can say
questions.explanation: Fire lanes are never blocked, not for an hour and not with permission. A fire engine needs the whole lane.

questions.q: Cubby flags a cylinder-lock unit Overlock Needed. Where does the overlock go?
options: In place of the tenant's core
On the hallway door for that row
questions.explanation: The overlock is added beside the tenant's lock, in the second hole or as a lockout plug. The tenant's core stays where it is.

questions.q: On a facility-managed cylinder-lock site, a tenant lost her only key. What happens?
options: The manager cuts it with a witness
ID check, then a core change
She waits until the lease ends
She drills it out and buys a new one
questions.explanation: On a cylinder site a lost key is a core change: she proves who she is on the account and the manager swaps the core. Nothing is cut or drilled.

lessons.title: Greens Fees and Charges
lessons.summary: Every fee Greens charges at its California sites, what each one is for, when it posts, and what to tell a customer.

lessons.title: Greens Tenant Protection
lessons.summary: How Cubby records protection, Greens' plan levels, the tasks that keep it current, and how to offer it at every move-in.

questions.q: A tenant's rent is $180 a month. On the 11th, what late fee should you see on the ledger?
questions.explanation: At $100 or more the fee is the greater of $20 or 15% of rent. 15% of $180 is $27, which is more than $20.

questions.q: A tenant's rent is $120 a month. What late fee should Cubby post on the 11th?
questions.explanation: 15% of $120 is $18, but at $100 or more the fee is the greater of $20 or 15%, so $20.

questions.q: A unit rents for exactly $100 a month. What is its late fee?
questions.explanation: $100 is in the top band, not the over-$60-under-$100 band. 15% is $15, so the greater, $20, applies.

questions.q: Ten 5x10s have a street rate of $50. All are rented: eight pay $50, one pays $45 and one is free to a charity. What is economic occupancy?
questions.explanation: Rent achieved is 8 x $50 + $45 + $0 = $445 of a possible $500, so 89%. Unit occupancy is still 100%.

questions.q: A Valley Center tenant says Greens' protection plan is the same thing as insurance. Under California law, she is right.
questions.explanation: California's Supreme Court has held a protection plan is not insurance. That is why staff never call it insurance.

questions.q: A tenant signs a California agreement on 02/10/2026. What must page one show about rent?
options: Every past rate for the unit
questions.explanation: SB 709 applies to agreements signed on or after 01/01/2026: page one shows whether the rate can change and the most it could reach in the first 12 months.

questions.q: A Valley Center contractor wants a unit. Which use is allowed?
options: Running a saw off unit power
questions.explanation: Store yes, operate no. Customers, employees, repairs and running equipment in the unit are running a business from it.

questions.q: A customer moving into Escondido asks about a security deposit. On a new move-in, Greens charges none.
questions.explanation: No deposit and no reservation fee on new move-ins. Only some leases brought over at Fairfield carry a deposit.

questions.q: Cubby raises Remind Tenant of POI Obligation on a lease. What do you do?
options: Post a late fee on the lease
Ask for the new policy details
Enroll the tenant in our plan
Overlock the unit until they call
questions.explanation: POI is proof of insurance: it is missing or expired. Call for the current policy number and expiration date. Enrolling is for a lapsed policy, after a call.

questions.q: A new Escondido customer picks the $2,500 level. Which price do you quote?
questions.explanation: New tenants pay today's price. The lower price is kept only on leases brought over from the previous system.

questions.q: Put these California lien steps in order.
options: Preliminary Lien Notice to the tenant and the alternate
Termination date passes; the lien attaches
Notice of Lien Sale with a blank Declaration in Opposition
questions.explanation: Notice first, then at least 14 days to the termination date, then the sale notice with its blank Declaration, at least 14 more days with advertising, then the sale.

questions.q: A Valley Center tenant pays half his balance on the 18th. At Greens, that stops the delinquency ladder.
questions.explanation: Only payment in full stops it. Cubby applies money to the oldest charge first, so the lease stays past due. Tell him the full amount.

questions.q: A certified envelope arrives at Temecula holding a signed Declaration in Opposition for a unit set for sale. What happens?
options: The sale goes ahead on schedule
Stop; it goes to your manager
Call the tenant to check it is real
File it and move the sale up
questions.explanation: A valid Declaration stops a California sale; Greens must go to court instead. It goes to your manager the same day.

questions.q: A Murrieta boat tenant reaches day 61 unpaid. What path does the boat take?
questions.explanation: Vehicles and boats are never sold in the unit auction. The day-61 task starts the vehicle path, taught in Vehicle and Boat Liens.

questions.q: A Fairfield tenant 25 days behind says he just got back from deployment. What do you do?
options: Carry on; he is home now
Ask him to waive his rights by phone
questions.explanation: The SCRA protects him during service and for 90 days after, without a court order. Record it, stop, and call your manager the same day.

questions.q: The morning of an online auction, a tenant's attorney emails a bankruptcy case number. What do you do?
options: Ask the tenant to pay first
Wait for the court to call
questions.explanation: A filing creates an automatic stay the moment it is filed: stop the sale, the calls and the fees, and tell your manager.

questions.q: At 9:00 AM on the 11th, an unpaid tenant says his gate code stopped working overnight. Why?
options: His code expires after a year
questions.explanation: At 12:00 AM on the 11th Cubby posts the late fee and changes the gate code. Take the payment, then check the code works.

questions.q: After a California lien sale, $300 is left once the balance and sale costs are paid. What happens to it?
options: Held a year for the tenant
questions.explanation: A lien sale is not a profit center. California holds a surplus one year for the tenant, then pays it to the county. Two years is Texas.

questions.q: On sale morning, the tenant calls to pay her full balance. What do you do?
options: Too late; the auction is already open
Take it; the unit is pulled
Take it, but the sale still runs
questions.explanation: Up to the sale, payment in full gets the unit back. Take it in Cubby and tell your manager at once so the unit comes out of the auction.

questions.q: A daughter says her father, a tenant, died last week and asks to get into his unit. What is needed first?
options: Nothing; close family always has access
Her photo ID and the unit number
questions.explanation: A family member does not automatically get access. A death certificate plus proof of authority over the estate, reviewed by your manager.

lessons.summary: Who may hear about an account, how to confirm a caller, how to answer police and process servers, and what Greens keeps.

lessons.summary: Greens' sites, spaces, prices, fees, ladder days and length of stay in one place, with the date they were read.

lessons.title: Words to Know
lessons.summary: Every word the Storage Academy uses, grouped by subject, one line each.

questions.q: A caller asks if Greens is "part of Public Storage." What best describes Greens?
options: A franchise of a national brand
questions.explanation: Greens owns and runs its own sites with its own policies: a private regional operator. Public Storage is a REIT.

questions.q: A friend asks you about Greens' Texas stores. Whose procedures do they run on?
questions.explanation: Austin, Sachse and Georgetown are run by CubeSmart on CubeSmart's own system and rules. They are not in Cubby.

questions.q: A Fairfield caller wants a 10x10 for household goods. What is the honest answer?
options: Book a Fairfield 10x10 and hope one opens
Say Greens has no units at all
Tell him to call Public Storage
questions.explanation: Fairfield is nearly all parking. Be honest about what the site offers and point to the Greens sites with units.

questions.q: A tenant says she "only needs it for a month," and declines autopay. What does experience say?
options: She will leave within a month
She should rent the largest unit
questions.explanation: Tenants stay far longer than they plan. Recommend protection and autopay anyway.

questions.q: A tenant pays $129 a month and stays 18 months. About how much rent is that?
questions.explanation: $129 x 18 = $2,322. One rental is worth thousands, which is why every call matters.

questions.q: A woman calling about a unit says she is leaving her marriage. What helps most?
options: Ask her spouse to call too
questions.explanation: Ask about the stuff, not the story. Discretion matters: she may not want anyone to know where her things are.

questions.q: A caller asks for "a 10x10 for my boat." What do you do?
options: Say Greens takes no boats at all
questions.explanation: A boat does not go in a standard unit. Switch to parking and ask its length on the trailer.

questions.q: A customer asks whether your climate building keeps humidity low. Your manager has confirmed only that the temperature is regulated. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Say what the building does and nothing more. Never promise humidity control or a temperature you have not confirmed.

questions.q: A Valley Center caller wants a mailbox. Which one-time charge applies?
options: A security deposit for the key
questions.explanation: A mailbox carries its own Mailbox Administration Fee instead of the unit admin fee. Greens charges no deposit or reservation fee.

questions.q: A Murrieta move-in is almost done. Which still belong on the move-in checklist? Pick all that apply.
options: A copy of the tenant's key
questions.explanation: Military status, the California alternate contact and the protection choice set up everything later, including the lien process. Greens never holds a tenant's key.

questions.q: A truck bends a steel post at a building corner. What is the right view of it?
options: It did its job; report it
Leave it until it falls over
Bill the driver and leave it bent
questions.explanation: A bollard is meant to take the hit the wall would take. A bent one did its job; report it for replacement.

questions.q: On your walk, the gate stops halfway and reverses. You find a stone in the track. What do you do?
options: Clear it and test the gate
Prop the gate open all day
questions.explanation: A stone in the track is yours to clear; then watch it cycle. A motor, sensor or controller fault goes to the gate company.

questions.q: A tenant on the second floor says her unit "has no ceiling, so anyone could climb in." What is true?
questions.explanation: Partitions stop below the roof and wire mesh closes the gap: nobody climbs through, and sprinklers and air reach the unit.

questions.q: A tenant who runs an extension cord from a hallway outlet into his unit is within the rules if the cord is heavy-duty.
questions.explanation: Units have no outlet of their own. A cord to a unit breaks the lease and is a fire risk.

questions.q: A tenant asks whether he can reach his unit after the office closes. At Greens sites, gate hours run longer than office hours.
questions.explanation: Gate hours are when tenants can get in; office hours are when staff are there. Gate hours are longer. Tell new tenants both.

questions.q: A new tenant asks which lock to buy. Which do you recommend?
options: No lock; the gate is enough
questions.explanation: A disc lock hides its shackle, so bolt cutters cannot grip it. A padlock's shackle is exposed and easy to cut.

questions.q: A tenant lost the key to his padlock and asks for the lock to be cut. Which belong to an authorized cut? Pick all that apply.
options: His signed authorization after an ID check
questions.explanation: Every cut has the authorization, a witness, photos and a new facility lock. Nothing inside is ever kept.

questions.q: After a break-in, what must happen to the camera footage?
options: Post it to find the thief
questions.explanation: Footage is overwritten after a set number of days. Tell your manager right away so it is saved. Never show it to the public.

questions.q: Why is the control key on a cylinder-lock site signed out and never lent?
options: It is the only key the tenant has
questions.explanation: It pulls the core from any cylinder lock, so it opens every cylinder door. A lost control key means a site-wide re-key.

questions.q: A Fairfield RV tenant calls at 6:00 AM on the 12th: the gate will not open. He has a balance from the 1st. What do you do?
options: Tell him the timing is the law
Overlock his space as well today
questions.explanation: Explain the account is past due, take the payment, then check the code works. Never give out a master code or defend the timing as law.

questions.q: A tenant's rent is $75 a month. What late fee should Cubby post on the 11th?
questions.explanation: Over $60 and under $100 is a flat $15. 15% applies only from $100.

questions.q: A storage unit rents for $55 a month. What is its late fee?
questions.explanation: $60 or less is $10. The 15% rule applies only from $100.

questions.q: A site has 200 units and 100 are rented, but the rented ones make up 80% of the square feet. What is physical occupancy?
questions.explanation: Physical occupancy counts square feet: 80%. Unit occupancy, counting doors, is 50%.

questions.q: A Temecula tenant hears his neighbor pays less for the same space and asks why. What do you say?
questions.explanation: In-place rates differ because rates change over time. Never discuss another tenant's rate, and send exception requests to your manager.

questions.q: A tenant wants you to promise her rent will never go up again. What do you say?
options: "I'll lock your rate for a year."
questions.explanation: Storage is month-to-month and rates change with notice. In California page one shows the 12-month maximum; point to it.

questions.q: A tenant points to a charge on her ledger that is not on Greens Fees and Charges. What do you do?
options: Explain it as you think best
Tell her every fee in Cubby is legal
questions.explanation: Never guess about a fee. Open the ledger with your manager.

questions.q: A new tenant says, "The facility is insured, so my things are covered." What is true?
questions.explanation: Greens' insurance covers its buildings and liability, not the tenant's belongings. That is why every lease has protection.

questions.q: A tenant files a claim after a leak and asks, "This is covered, right?" What do you say?
questions.explanation: Only the claims administrator decides. Never promise a claim, and never call the plan insurance.

questions.q: A Temecula RV owner's motorhome is normally protected by his own vehicle insurance, not by a storage protection plan.
questions.explanation: Vehicles, RVs and boats carry the owner's own vehicle or boat insurance. Record the policy number and expiration date.

questions.q: An existing Escondido tenant on an older lease asks what her plan costs. What do you quote?
options: What Cubby shows on her lease
The higher of the two prices in Cubby
questions.explanation: Quote what Cubby shows for an existing tenant, and never change a lease's price on your own.

questions.q: A Temecula move-in gives only a phone number. What else do you collect?
options: A spouse's signature on page one
questions.explanation: Lien notices go to the last known address, and in California the agreement must request an alternate contact. Missing details break the lien process later.

questions.q: A Valley Center tenant asks to keep a camping stove and a gas can in his unit. What do you say?
questions.explanation: Gasoline and propane are prohibited: fire and explosion risk to everyone on the property.

questions.q: A tenant asks why part of a Texas storage agreement is in bold. Texas requires the lien language to be underlined or in bold for a sale without a court.
questions.explanation: Texas Property Code 59.041: without underlined or conspicuous bold lien language, the facility cannot sell without a court judgment.

questions.q: A boat tenant pays $184 by autopay; it fails on the 1st and nothing is paid by the 11th. What late fee posts?
questions.explanation: 15% of $184 is $27.60, more than $20. In full, she would owe $211.60 to stop the ladder.

questions.q: It is the 2nd. What is the most valuable thing you can do on the delinquency ladder today?
options: Change the late payers' gate codes
questions.explanation: The early calls stop most delinquencies before any fee posts. Overlocks and notices come later, and Cubby handles codes.

questions.q: You reach an unpaid tenant on the 6th. What do you never do on the call?
options: Confirm who you're speaking to first
questions.explanation: Never leave a balance or lien detail on a voicemail, text or email unless Greens' policy says so. The others are the call done right.

questions.q: In California, how long must rent be unpaid before the Preliminary Lien Notice may go out?
questions.explanation: 14 consecutive days unpaid (21703). Ten days is the late-fee rule.

questions.q: A California preliminary notice must go out today for a tenant who signed email consent. Which delivery methods are lawful? Pick all that apply.
options: First-class mail with a certificate of mailing
Email, with the consent and proof of delivery
A note on the unit door
questions.explanation: Certified mail, first-class with a certificate of mailing, or consented email with proof of delivery, to the tenant and the alternate.

questions.q: A friend in Texas asks when the storage lien attaches to her things there. What is right?
questions.explanation: In Texas the lien attaches when property is placed in the facility (59.006). California's attaches on the termination date.

questions.q: A coworker wants to clear "obvious trash" from a unit before buyers see it at the sale. What do you do?
options: Help, to get a better price
questions.explanation: Nothing leaves a liened unit outside the process, before or after the sale.

questions.q: Your cousin wants to bid on a Greens lien sale online from home. That is fine because it is a public auction.
questions.explanation: Staff never bid and never let friends or family bid at a Greens lien sale, online or in person.

questions.q: A Greens site honestly did not know a tenant was on active duty and sold his unit without a court order. Under the SCRA that honest mistake is excused.
questions.explanation: The Department of Justice treats the SCRA as strict liability: honest mistakes are no defense. Check military status before every sale.

questions.q: Which mean you stop the ladder and call your manager the same day? Pick all that apply.
questions.explanation: Each of these can make the sale unlawful or the amount wrong. A payment on the 2nd is the ladder working.

questions.q: On your walk, a unit Cubby shows as vacant has a tenant's lock on it. What do you do?
options: Ignore it until the month-end report
questions.explanation: It may be unauthorized use. Photograph it, check the cameras with your manager and follow the process. Never cut it yourself.

questions.q: The cash drawer is $20 short at close. What do you do?
questions.explanation: Recount with your manager and check every receipt against Cubby. Never cover it from your pocket or change the report.

questions.q: Put these vacant unit steps in order.
options: Confirm the lock and contents are gone
Check the door and look for damage
Mark the unit rent-ready in Cubby
questions.explanation: Confirm empty, photograph, clean, check, lock, then mark rent-ready so it can be sold.

questions.q: At 7:00 AM you see someone inside the fence cutting a lock. What do you do?
questions.explanation: Never confront a thief. Go somewhere safe, lock the office, call 911, then your manager, and note what you saw from safety.

questions.q: A storm flooded the low row of drive-up units. What do you do before any cleanup?
questions.explanation: Photograph inside and out first; photos are evidence for insurance and tenants' claims. No tenants into a damaged building until cleared.

questions.q: A customer slips in a wet hallway and hurts her wrist. Where do you document it?
questions.explanation: Every incident is written up the same day through Fill a Form in Nexus: what, when, where, who, what you did, photos, follow-up.

questions.q: A caller says, "My husband rents there. What's his balance?" She is not on the account. What do you say?
options: "I can't share if he's a customer."
"He's in 1142, but I can't say more."
questions.explanation: Even the fact that he rents is private. Say the same sentence, kindly, every time.

questions.q: A caller says she is the tenant and asks you to confirm her unit number before she pays. What do you do?
questions.explanation: The caller gives the identifying details; you never read them out first. In doubt, call back at the number on file.

questions.q: A facility has 320 units. How many accessible units does the 2010 ADA Standards table require?
questions.explanation: Over 200: 10 plus 2% of the units over 200. 10 + 2% of 120 = 12.4, rounded up to 13.

questions.q: A facility has 180 units. How many accessible units are required?
questions.explanation: Up to 200 units: 5%, at least one. 5% of 180 is 9.

questions.q: A customer asks whether Greens "rents to people without papers." What is right?
options: Ask about nationality only when unsure
questions.explanation: Greens asks every customer for the same ID and information and never asks about immigration status or nationality.

questions.q: A subpoena arrives asking for a tenant's gate log for two weeks. What do you do?
options: Email the log to the sender
questions.explanation: Never ignore a subpoena. Send it to your manager the same day and ask that the records and footage be preserved.

questions.q: A site has 18 move-ins and 13 move-outs in a month. What are net rentals?
questions.explanation: Net rentals = move-ins minus move-outs: 18 - 13 = +5.

questions.q: A site bills $50,000 on the 1st and $4,000 is unpaid on the 10th. What is delinquency?
questions.explanation: $4,000 / $50,000 = 8%. Collecting half before the 11th brings it to 4%.

questions.q: A site gets 60 inquiries in a week and rents 15 units. What is the conversion rate?
questions.explanation: 15 / 60 = 25%. Faster callbacks raise it with no extra marketing.

questions.q: A coworker says Valley Center and Escondido have far more enclosed units in Cubby than the storage-unit count. Why?
questions.explanation: Cubby counts mailboxes as units. Greens by the Numbers counts storage units and mailboxes separately.

questions.q: Your manager says a tenant's in-place rate is below street rate. What does that mean?
options: She pays less than new tenants
Her rent is locked below the legal cap
questions.explanation: In-place is what an existing tenant pays now; street rate is today's price for a new customer.
